residentHome: sein Bezirk: die Stadt im Körper, auf Streife von Abteilung zu Abteilung
structure: cyborg cop's patrol through his district; card beats in Alice mechanics (name, image, claim); his zero-tolerance ideology and false assumptions break on the cards; failure loop: nightly report to a president who never answers; the memo reveals there is only a press secretary; outro from card images
synopsis: A spoken-word number from a card deck that describes the human body as a city. It is performed by a small armored police cyborg on patrol through that city, for whoever happens to be there.
bestOfReason: District 1, 2: the city runs itself, the citizen was never asked.
Patrol 5, 7, 10, 28: the departments that need no police.
His unit 11, 17, 19: memory, the fire that burns the city, friendly fire.
Threats inside 15, 18: copy errors and the competitor.
His training 20: built as a teenager.
Cold cases 21, 23, 24, 30: looking beats the book; the institution rejects the finding; the quack stays on the payroll.
His method 26: guessing to fill the gap.
Turn 6: no president, only a press secretary.
Landing 32: the body keeps the score.

omitted.3: manual card overlaps the cop's rulebook joke

orderReason: Patrol order: district, departments, alarm (immune → inflammation → autoimmune), inside threats (DNA → cancer), training (thymus), cold cases, method (blind eye), memo (brain), score.

songLineChanges.songLine: The decision was already underway five hundred milliseconds before you made it.
The Lungs: seventy square meters folded into your chest.
Eighty percent of the phone calls go up to the brain.

cues.cue: police radio squelch on the backbeat

beats: Unit Nine, Biological Metropolis Police. Step behind the line. Whoever you are, you're in my district now.
Zero tolerance, full surveillance, every visitor a suspect. Every night I file my report to the president upstairs. He has never written back.

beats.text: The City Inside, a rabbit cross-section revealing an industrial cityscape. It has been running the civilization while you were busy.
The Citizen, a hydra of animals erupting from the neck. You never once told this city what to do; it never once asked your permission.
beats.post: No permit for that. I let it slide.

beats.text: The Heart, a badger on a massive drum kit. The brain can modify the rate; the brain cannot generate it. The badger drums alone.
beats.post: No license for the noise. I wrote it up.

beats.text: The Lungs, two giant broccoli trees exchanging blue and red birds: seventy square meters folded into your chest, the only manual override.
beats.post: The one door with a manual override. I keep my hand near it.

beats.text: The Gut, zombie commuters boarding: eighty percent of the phone calls go up to the brain. The subway runs the city.
beats.post: Not one of them has a ticket. I checked.

beats.text: The Night Shift, mice in janitor overalls cleaning inside a glowing skull. Sleep is the janitorial shift washing the thoughts out of the carpet.
beats.post: I stay awake. Somebody has to.

beats.text: The Immune System, armored rats with riot shields spotlighting a virus. A library of every murder attempt. It remembers things you have forgotten.
Inflammation, a fire salamander with a flamethrower: the response that heals the wound becomes the mechanism that burns the city.
beats.post: Block saved. Block gone. The paperwork says success.

beats.text: Autoimmune, a crazed dog biting itself: the discrimination fails, not the weapon. The gun works fine; it's just pointed the wrong way.

beats.pre: The real threat is already inside:
beats.text: DNA Replication, a black spider weaving a double helix web: one error per billion letters. You have had cancer many times; the spider usually eats it.
beats.post: The spider has no badge, and a better record than mine.

beats.text: Cancer, a giant crab with a fortress built on its shell. Evolution occurring inside you. It is not a disease; it is a competitor.
The Aging Thymus, an old elephant in a crumbling library. Your immune repertoire was built when you were a teenager. Hope you read good books.

beats: Upstairs they keep cold-case files on the troublemakers.

beats.text: Andreas Vesalius, a mole in an Elizabethan ruff stomping on a Galen textbook: he looked at the body instead of the book. Everyone else was wrong.
Ignaz Semmelweis, a raccoon washing his hands in a lime bucket while silhouettes mock: he saved the mothers. The doctors committed him.
beats.post: I'd have arrested him too. Disturbing the peace.

beats.text: The Semmelweis Problem, a barn door bursting open with rays of light: the evidence is available, the implication is uncomfortable, we reject the finding.
The Humoralist, a tortoise carrying four potion bottles, one spilling: wrong in the facts, right in the vibe. It was the first Kayfabe.
The Blind Eye: you have a hole in your vision. The brain fills it in with best guesses. Trust, but verify.

beats: Then the president finally answered. A memo.

beats.text: The Brain, five owls in judge wigs arguing over a burning map: the decision was already underway five hundred milliseconds before you made it. You are the press secretary, not the president.

beats: So there's nobody upstairs. Just a spokesman. I filed my report anyway.

beats.text: The Scorekeeper, a sea urchin writing with a feather quill in a leather-bound ledger: the body keeps the score because the body is the score.

beats: Night shift, district nine: the badger drums, the mice mop, the spider eats the errors, and the cop with the minigun writes a report nobody reads.
